title: Abstract 1133: Risk effect of primary prevention strategy with aspirin on lung cancer incidence depends on high-level use, bodyweight and age: A U.S. adults evidence

sections.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title> <jats:p>Chemoprevention of cancer with aspirin is of particular interest as a primary prevention strategy, which was still in controversial. Using 101,462 individual participants' data from a U.S. adult's cohort, Cox regression model was used to detect the aspirin dosage effect on lung cancer risk. We calculated the effects of irregular use, low-dose use, and high-dose use of aspirin on lung cancer risk in population stratified by bodyweight and age. High-dose use of aspirin raised up 28% risk of lung cancer compared to no use (HR = 1.28, 95%CI = [1.14-1.45], P = 3.37×10-5). Meanwhile, the risk effect of high-dose aspirin significantly decreased with bodyweight increasing, indicating an antagonistic interaction (HRinteraction = 0.96, 95%CI = [0.94-0.99], P = 1.26×10-2). Furthermore, for these participants prone to lung cancer with bodyweight less than 80 kg, high-dose aspirin usage showed an elevated risk if their age less than 76 (HRage≤76 = 1.47, 95%CI = [1.25-1.73], P = 3.81×10-6), but did not exhibit risk effect in elders (HRage>76 = 1.13, 95%CI = [0.46-2.69], P = 0.80). The three-way interaction among dose of aspirin, bodyweight and age indicated that these vulnerable people (age ≤76 years and bodyweight <80 kg) with high lung cancer risk should be cautious to use high-dose aspirin for lung cancer chemoprevention.</jats:p> <jats:p>Citation Format: Xuesi Dong.
